overall: The AG found the Planning Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: the notice topic "Town Meeting zoning articles" was specific enough. Claims against Planning Department and Town Planner were declined as non-public bodies; a Host Community Agreement claim was withdrawn. No orders issued.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the February 13 meeting notice was not detailed enough because it did not name the specific zoning articles to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: we find the notice topic “Discussion: Town Meeting zoning articles” was sufficiently detailed to inform the public of the anticipated nature of the discussion where the Chair anticipated that the Town Planner would present proposed zoning articles to the Board and the Chair did not anticipate any particular zoning articles would be discussed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Planning Department and the Town Planner violated the Open Meeting Law; these are not public bodies under the Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law applies only to public bodies and their members; therefore, we decline to review any allegations that the Planning Department or Town Planner violated the Law.

allegations.summary: Original complaint included an allegation about a Host Community Agreement, which the complainant later withdrew.
allegations.key_passage: In subsequent communications, the Complainant informed our office that he no longer wished to pursue this additional allegation.
